abstract: Responding to service failures represents an acid test at organizational frontlines, where human service agents, alongside a growing share of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered service agents, engage in service recovery. Particularly when recovery outcomes are only partially favorable, customers may perceive these decisions as unclear or difficult to understand, potentially impairing their evaluation of the service encounter. This raises the question of whether explanations of service recovery decisions should be provided and, if so, how and by whom. Addressing this practical need and the related research gap, the article examines the effects of service recovery explanations on customers’ post-recovery reactions. Across three main studies and three supplementary studies spanning multiple service industries, the authors demonstrate that service recovery explanations can enhance customer satisfaction and choice by fostering perceptions of agent competence and warmth. These beneficial effects, however, depend on key contingencies: rationales outperform excuses and justifications, specific explanations tend to be more effective than general ones, and explanations provided by AI service agents can be more impactful than those delivered by human service agents. Overall, the article advances understanding of service recovery communication and offers actionable guidance for managing both AI- and human-mediated service recovery.

ur.ai_reason: AI服务代理与人工服务补救对比，多项研究
ur.tldr: 研究服务失败后补救解释对客户反应的影响，跨三项主研究与三项补充研究。发现补救解释通过提升客户对服务方能力与温暖感的感知，增强其满意度和再次选择意愿；但效果受关键调节因素制约：理性归因优于借口与辩护，具体解释优于笼统解释，且由AI服务 agent 提供的解释效果反而可能优于人类服务 agent。

title: Managing Critical Frontline Agent–Customer Interactions: The Role of Service Recovery Explanations Across Artificial Intelligence and Human Agents
title_zh: 管理关键一线客服与客户互动：服务补救解释在人工智能与人类客服中的作用
